neighbours.label: the verb or negation right where a feasibility judgement of an activity is due ('doing X may not be [possible]', 'has proven [to be difficult]')
fire: Keeping every customer happy during a product recall may not be possible.
Translating the poem without losing its rhythm has proven to be very hard.
Restoring the fresco to its original colours will be extremely difficult.
Crossing the desert on foot in midsummer would be nearly impossible.
Finding a cheap flat near the centre has become almost impossible.
Teaching the whole syllabus in six weeks is simply not feasible.
Removing the stain from the old silk turned out to be quite tricky.
Reaching every village before the monsoon will not be easy.
quiet: Keeping every customer happy during a product recall is our main goal.
The translated poem has proven to be very popular.
The restored fresco will be shown to the public in May.
The desert in midsummer would be nearly empty of tourists.
The cheap flat near the centre has become very noisy.
The whole syllabus is printed in the student handbook.
The old silk turned out to be quite valuable.
Reaching every village before the monsoon means leaving at dawn.

notes: Card: peaks on ' be', ' become', ' is', ' proven', ' не' before possible/difficult/challenging with an activity as subject; the + pole promotes ' feasible', ' possible', ' done', ' impossible'. Probes: 0.51-0.64 for activity + feasibility predicate, 0.45 for 'this was not possible'; 'has proven to be quite reliable' 0.00, 'will be painted' 0.03, gerund + 'means' 0.16. Near misses keep the verb frame and change what is being judged.
